claims.explanation: Triptolide covalently inhibits XPB/ERCC3, a TFIIH subunit required for RNA polymerase II transcription and nucleotide excision repair, causing rapid RNAPII degradation and transcriptional arrest. Selectivity likely reflects dependence on high transcriptional output and intact DNA-repair/transcription-coupled repair capacity, so tumors with high ERCC3/XPB expression or NER proficiency are more sensitive, while those with low transcription factor availability or apoptosis resistance are protected.

features.basis: XPB is the direct covalent target of triptolide; higher target expression increases drug engagement
RNA polymerase II is the downstream effector; high transcriptional demand increases dependence on Pol II activity
TP53 mutations are enriched in selectively killed lines, consistent with impaired DNA-damage/apoptotic checkpoints after transcription inhibition
Anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family signaling is a known resistance mechanism to apoptosis-inducing cancer therapies
Mcl-1 overexpression confers resistance to apoptosis and is a key resistance target in cancer therapy
Loss of caspase-mediated apoptosis signaling reduces sensitivity to transcription-inhibition-induced cell death
Caspase mutations and deregulated apoptosis are linked to therapy chemoresistance
Virtual cell shows NFKBIA downregulation after triptolide, and NF-kB inhibition by triptolide is a known anti-inflammatory/antitumor mechanism
Triptolide is annotated to target RELA/NF-kB; high NF-kB activity may support survival and reduce sensitivity
SF3B1 mutations appear in several selectively killed lines and may alter splicing/transcription coupling
BRAF-mutant melanoma and other BRAF-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines, possibly via MAPK-driven transcriptional addiction
PTEN loss appears in multiple sensitive lines and may impair DNA repair/apoptosis regulation
